trip.title: Vellmoor & the Tide Coast
trip.subtitle: Three days, with the times that matter
trip.intro:
Vellmoor is a small harbour city that turns its back on the wind: the old town climbs away from the quays in terraces, and almost everything you want is within a forty-minute walk. This plan keeps mornings for the things that need an early start, leaves the afternoons loose, and never books two timed entries on the same day.

Tides matter here. The sea baths and the Sallow Island ferry both run to the tide table, so the third day is built around it.

tide-museum.name: Museum of Tide & Trade
tide-museum.tagline: Three floors on how a town lived by the sea.
tide-museum.editorial: Working tide engine, ship models and a chart room, in a former customs house on the quay.

note.why_you: You said the last museum you loved was the one with a working machine in it. This one has a tide engine the size of a room, and it runs on the hour.
note.what_to_do: Top floor first (the chart room, quiet before eleven), then down to the engine for the 10:00 run. The ship models on the ground floor are skippable unless it is raining.
note.what_to_skip: The temporary exhibition on the stairs — a fee on top and twenty minutes you will want at the quay.
note.best_time: Opening time on a weekday. By noon the school groups arrive.
note.tickets: Timed entry, booked for 9:30. The ticket is good for a second visit within seven days — useful if the island day is rained off.
note.accessibility: Lift to every floor; the engine gallery has a rail and benches.

reviews.author: Marit Olsén
reviews.text: Went for the tide engine and stayed two hours. Ask the attendant about the 1911 flood marks — they are not on any sign.

sources.title: Museum of Tide & Trade — plan your visit
Ostenia Weekly — 'An hour with the tide engine'

lantern-quay.name: Lantern Quay Market
lantern-quay.tagline: Fish, cheese and whatever came off the boats.

note.why_you: Half of what you asked for was 'somewhere to eat standing up'. This is it.
note.what_to_do: Walk the length once without buying, then back to the smoked-fish stalls at the east end. The cheese man (blue awning) closes at one.
note.what_to_skip: The souvenir row by the car park.
note.best_time: Before noon; the fish is gone by two.

sources.title: Lantern Quay traders' association — stall list

quillet.name: Quillet's
quillet.tagline: Soup, bread, one fish dish, done by two.

note.why_you: Vegetable-led, quiet, no music — the three things you listed.
note.what_to_do: Whatever the soup is. Share the fish.

saint-aurel.name: Saint Aurel's Belfry
saint-aurel.tagline: 212 steps to the best view of the harbour.

note.why_you: You climbed the tower in every city on the last trip. This is the one here.
note.what_to_do: Pay at the door, climb to the bell loft (160 steps), decide there whether to do the last flight. Ten minutes at the top is enough; the walk down is the view.
note.best_time: Mid-afternoon in November — the sun is low over the islands by three.
note.tickets: Cash or card at the door; no booking.
note.accessibility: Steps only; the loft has a bench.

sources.title: Saint Aurel's — belfry opening and safety notes

rookwell.name: Rookwell Old Town walk
rookwell.tagline: Steps, courts and almshouses — a loop of about 2 km.
rookwell.address: Start at Gull Steps, Rookwell, Vellmoor

note.why_you: No tickets, no queue, and it ends at your door.
note.what_to_do: Gull Steps up, left along Tanners' Court, through the almshouse garden (gate is open until five), down Weaver's Lane to the sea wall, and back along it to the inn.
note.what_to_skip: The 'historic' pub on Weaver's Lane — new in 2019.
note.accessibility: Steep steps at the start; the sea-wall half is flat.

sources.title: Vellmoor Civic Society — Rookwell walk leaflet (PDF)

brine-house.name: The Brine House
brine-house.tagline: Fish from the quay, cooked plainly.

note.why_you: The one booking that was hard to get; it is the room, not just the food.
note.what_to_do: Ask for the window table; order the day's fish and the burnt-butter potatoes.

cinder-lane.name: Cinder Lane Bakery
cinder-lane.tagline: Cardamom buns and a proper flat white.

note.why_you: Your kind of breakfast: good coffee, one good thing, no fuss.
note.what_to_do: Cardamom bun, flat white, the bench outside if it is dry.

hollin-terraces.name: Hollin Botanical Terraces
hollin-terraces.tagline: Seven terraces up the hill, a glasshouse at the top.
hollin-terraces.editorial: Hillside botanical garden with a Victorian glasshouse, a fern ravine and views over the harbour.

note.why_you: Gardens were the thing you rated highest after the last trip, and this one is on a hill, so it is also the view.
note.what_to_do: Tram to the top gate, walk the terraces downhill: fern ravine, the winter borders (they are the point in November), glasshouse last when it has warmed.
note.what_to_skip: The children's trail and the gift shop at the bottom gate.
note.best_time: Opening time; the terraces are in sun until about one.
note.tickets: At the gate, card. The day pass does not include it.
note.accessibility: A buggy runs the main path every half hour; the ravine path is steps.
note.food: Terrace Café on terrace three — soup, tarts, decent coffee.

sources.title: Hollin Terraces — what's in flower in November

glass-foundry.name: The Glass Foundry
glass-foundry.tagline: A working hot shop; you blow a glass of your own.

note.why_you: You wanted one thing to make, not just see. The 45-minute slot makes a tumbler you collect the next morning — or they post it.
note.what_to_do: Watch the 13:45 demonstration from the gallery, then your slot at 14:15. Collect Saturday after the baths, or pay the postage.
note.tickets: Workshop booked for 14:15; the demonstration is free with it.
note.accessibility: Ground floor, level access; the hot shop is loud and warm.

reviews.author: Tobias Rennick
reviews.text: Forty-five minutes, two instructors, and I came away with something I actually use. Book ahead — they take four people a slot.

mirrowdale.name: Mirrowdale Viewpoint
mirrowdale.tagline: The whole coast from one bench.

note.why_you: The late-light place. On a clear afternoon you can see the island you sail to on Saturday.
note.what_to_do: Bench first, then the ridge loop (25 minutes, waymarked, muddy after rain). Back on the 16:50 bus.
note.best_time: An hour before sunset (16:48 in mid-November).
note.accessibility: The viewpoint is a short level path from the bus stop; the loop is not.

sallow-island.name: Sallow Island
sallow-island.tagline: A chapel, a lighthouse path and a kiosk — forty minutes out.

note.why_you: You asked for one day that felt like being away from the city. This is the furthest the plan goes.
note.what_to_do: Chapel first (key at the kiosk), the lighthouse path out and back (50 minutes), crab roll at the kiosk, the 13:15 home.
note.what_to_skip: The 'seal trip' touts on the pier — the seals are on the rocks you walk past anyway.
note.best_time: The morning sailing; the afternoon one is the busy one on Saturdays.
note.tickets: Buy at the kiosk on Lantern Quay once the 08:00 confirmation is up.
note.accessibility: The pier has a ramp; the lighthouse path is rough and not for wheels.

sources.title: Sallow Island ferry — November sailings and weather policy

harbour-baths.name: Harbour Baths
harbour-baths.tagline: A heated sea-water pool on the quay, and a cold one.

note.why_you: A swim was on the list every time; this is the one that works in November.
note.what_to_do: Heated pool, then the cold plunge if you dare, then the sauna (Saturdays). Seventy-five minutes is plenty.
note.tickets: Walk in; towels for hire; lockers take a coin you get back.
note.best_time: Early afternoon on Saturday, when the water is highest and the morning swimmers have gone.
note.accessibility: Pool hoist available; ask at the desk.

reviews.author: Ines Varga
reviews.text: Warm pool, cold sea, hot sauna — in that order. Weekends get busy after three.

fennick.name: Fennick & Daughters
fennick.tagline: Three floors; the travel room is at the top.

note.why_you: Every trip ends in a bookshop. This is the good one.
note.what_to_do: Travel room upstairs; the local-history shelf by the window. They post abroad.
note.best_time: Late afternoon, when the day is done.

corran-arcade.name: Corran Arcade
corran-arcade.tagline: A glass-roofed arcade of makers' shops, across the river.

note.why_you: Makers' shops under glass — a dry half day when the weather turns.

ninefold-steps.name: The Ninefold Steps
ninefold-steps.tagline: Nine flights of stone from the river to the old walls.

note.why_you: The classic walk up; closed for repairs this month.

items.label: Day pass
items.text: Tram and bus, 24 hours from first use, bought on the tram (card). Covers both bus 11 rides on Friday.

items.label: Ferry
items.text: Sallow Island ferry from Lantern Quay; buy at the kiosk, cash or card. Sailings follow the tide — the November table is in the sources.

items.label: Walking
items.text: Everything in the old town is on steps or cobbles; the sea wall is flat and lit until midnight.

items.label: Currency
items.text: Ostenian crown. Cards almost everywhere; the island kiosk and the market stalls want cash.

items.label: Booked already
items.text: Tide Museum timed entry (Thu 9:30), Glass Foundry workshop (Fri 14:15), The Brine House dinner (Thu 19:00).

items.label: Not booked
items.text: Harbour Baths (walk-in), ferry (buy on the day once the sailing is confirmed).

practical.title: Weather in November
practical.text: Cool and changeable: 6–11 °C, wind off the sea most afternoons, light rain one day in three. A windproof layer matters more than an umbrella; the old town's lanes funnel the gusts.

items.label: Emergency
items.text: Dial 118 for police, fire or ambulance anywhere in Ostenia.

items.label: Pharmacy
items.text: Quay Street Pharmacy, open until 20:00 daily; the night rota is posted in its window.

items.label: The inn
items.text: Front desk until 22:00; a night bell after that.

items.label: High tide / low tide
items.text: Flod / ebb — you will see both on the ferry board

practical.title: Packing notes
practical.text: Swimsuits and a quick-dry towel for the baths; closed shoes for the foundry; a small cash float for the island; the museum ticket on your phone.
